transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, what brought me in is... I had a bit of an outburst recently. I blew up at one of the younger volunteers over a crooked tablecloth of all things. I just really lost my temper. And I don't usually talk to people that way, so it kind of bothered me. That's why I decided to come in.
Is this kind of intense reaction something that happens to you often in various situations, or is this way of behaving something that has only started recently?

No, it's definitely not something that happens to me often. I haven't been like this my whole life. It's very recent. I'd say this has really only been going on for about a week now... ever since the robbery outside the bank.
Since that robbery, have you been having any unwanted, distressing thoughts or memories about the event popping into your mind?

Yes, I have. It happens out of nowhere, really. I'll just be sitting at my kitchen table, minding my own business, and suddenly I hear that man's rough voice right in my head. Or I'll see the donation envelope hitting the ground again. It just pops up when I'm not even trying to think about it.
Aside from the robbery that happened a week ago, have you been experiencing these distressing thoughts or reactions for longer than a month?
No, no, nothing like that. Like I said, it's really just been this past week. Before the robbery, I was perfectly fine. I haven't had anything like this going on for a month, no.
